question: Can the two-scale five-island demographic pattern be partitioned into a regional sea-ice signal and a static island breeding-habitat filter?

source.title: Seasonal sea ice indices including timing of ice-edge advance/retreat, ice season duration and actual ice days for PAL LTER sub-regions
source.source_reference: Stammerjohn seasonal sea ice indices; package version 9
source.documented_ice_year: February/March-to-February/March sea-ice year; use dataset's own ice-year label

regional_lane.subregion_rule: use the North/South PAL LTER subregion spanning grid lines 600 to 200 when present; fail closed rather than substitute a different subregion
regional_lane.alignment_rule: ice-year beginning in calendar year y predicts breeding-population growth from census y to census y+1, so the complete ice season precedes the response census
regional_lane.primary_response: log1p(total breeding pairs across CHR,COR,HUM,LIT,TOR at y+1) - log1p(total at y)
regional_lane.island_response: same annual log1p growth per island, retained for heterogeneity diagnostics
regional_lane.direction: longer ice duration is predicted to be associated with less-negative / more-positive Adelie regional population growth
robustness: report effect sizes and uncertainty; no stepwise predictor search

local_lane.status: external replication, not fresh predictor discovery

source.citation: Fraser et al. 2013, A Nonmarine Source of Variability in Adelie Penguin Demography, Oceanography 26(3):207-209

local_lane.predictor: percent suboptimal breeding habitat based on southwest aspect under dominant northeasterly storm winds
local_lane.response: frozen 1991-2017 island-specific annual multiplicative population-change slope
local_lane.interpretation: This lane asks whether the previously published geomorphology ranking continues to predict decline rates in the independently extended 1991-2017 census result.

synthesis.supported_if: regional sea ice explains meaningful interannual variation in five-island total growth while suboptimal habitat predicts between-island long-term decline severity
synthesis.interpretation: shared marine forcing sets temporal direction while terrestrial island geometry modulates local vulnerability
not_allowed: claim sea ice is the only regional driver
claim habitat correlation proves snow accumulation caused every decline
claim local residual variation is competition
pool the five islands as statistically independent replicates of regional climate
